Parameter Descriptions for the Derived Verbs

Source: R/params.R
derived_params.Rd

Parameter descriptions shared by kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), and kb_predict_biomass_canopy().

Arguments

weight

A kb_fit_weight object.

wetdry

A kb_fit_wetdry object, required for dry, carbon, and nitrogen biomass, or NULL. All fits must be of the same species and have the same number of draws.

carbon

A kb_fit_carbon object, required for carbon biomass, or NULL.

nitrogen

A kb_fit_nitrogen object, required for nitrogen biomass, or NULL.

measure

A string, one of "wet", "dry", "carbon", or "nitrogen", giving the type of biomass to predict.

n_plants

A whole number of sizes averaged per draw to compute the mean plant weight; larger values are more precise and slower to compute.

progress

A string, one of "bar" (the default, a console progress bar) or "none" (silent).

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is shown for a site or year not in the fit. Sites and years in the fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "sample" (the default): a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. Rows that name the same new site or year, or that have no site or year column, share one effect; give new sites or years different names for independent effects. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

  • "average": the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

pool_by

A character vector naming character or factor columns to group the rows by, such as c("site", "year"), character(0) to pool all rows, or NULL (the default) for one estimate per input row. The rows of a group are combined on each draw as described in Details. To use a different summary method, such as an unweighted mean of rows, summarise the draws column, for example with posterior::rvar_mean().
